newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudan rebels say government colonel defects.
newsitem.headline: Sudan rebels say government colonel defects.

text.p: A Sudanese rebel group said on Wednesday a senior government officer had defected and joined rebel ranks in the war-torn south of the country.

Yassir Arman, spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) led by guerrilla leader John Garang, told Reuters that the officer with the rank of colonel joined rebel forces at the town of Damazine a few days ago.
"Colonel Al-Kana Tiger of the Sudanese Army defected from Damazine garrisons with some of his soldiers and joined our forces in Southern Blue Nile some days ago," said Arman.
Arman said the officer was in the headquarters of the commander of the rebel alliance in that area.
"He is the most senior officer to defect to our side to date," Arman added.
The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north.
